title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let pi = pi_{0,3}^ the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}. It is generated by inertia loops l_0, l_1 (and l_infinity). S_3 acts on it through the 3-cycle rho and the transposition sigma_infinity, which swaps l_0 and l_1.

The object studied. N_{0,3}^{!~} is the set of outer automorphisms of pi that commute with S_3 up to inner automorphisms and that normalise the inertia subgroup L_0 = closure of l_0^Z. The theorem on the previous page parametrises the lifts u_{(xi,eta)} by pairs (xi, eta) in pi with u(rho) = xi rho and u(sigma_infinity) = eta sigma_infinity. The pairs satisfy relation (133), a 3-cycle cocycle relation, and relation (134), a 2-cycle relation linked to the first by the 'loop formula' with multiplier nu in Z^, mu = 2nu+1. L_0 acts by (xi, eta) -> (l_0^n xi l_1^{-n}, l_0^n eta l_1^{-n}).

This page.
(1) Group law (138)-(139): the set of pairs gets the group structure transported from composition of automorphisms, (xi', eta')(xi, eta) = (u'(xi) xi', u'(eta) eta'). This is a crossed-homomorphism (cocycle) composition law, of the same type as Drinfeld's law (lambda_1, f_1)(lambda_2, f_2) = (lambda_1 lambda_2, f_1 · f_2(x^{lambda_1}, f_1^{-1} y^{lambda_1} f_1)).
(2) Corollary (140)-(142): every genuine automorphism u in M_{0,3}^{!~} can be written as u = int(f^{-1}) ∘ u_{(xi,eta)} with f in pi. It then satisfies u(sigma_infinity) = h sigma_infinity and u(rho) = g rho, where h = f^{-1} eta sigma_infinity(f) and g = f^{-1} xi rho(f). In other words the cocycle changes by a coboundary.
(3) Uniqueness (144): the representation is unique up to the L_0-action, with f' = l_0^n f.
(4) NB, elimination. The multiplier mu (equivalently nu) is already determined by xi; this is said to come from 'abelian' computations in GL(2,Z^)', i.e. images in the congruence quotient. Through (134), xi and eta determine each other: eta = xi l_1^{-nu}. The system therefore reduces to a single unknown:
- either xi with xi rho(xi) rho^2(xi) = 1 and (xi l_1^{-nu}) sigma_infinity(xi l_1^{-nu}) = 1, i.e. sigma_infinity(xi) = l_1^nu xi^{-1} l_0^nu;
- or eta with eta sigma_infinity(eta) = 1 and (eta l_1^nu) rho(eta l_1^nu) rho^2(eta l_1^nu) = 1.

Comparison with Drinfeld. With f = eta, x = l_0, y = l_1 and m = nu, the second form is exactly Drinfeld's relation (I), f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1, together with the hexagon (II), f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m f(x,y) x^m = 1, with lambda = 2m+1. So the page gives a self-contained derivation of the two- and three-cycle defining relations of GT^. The pentagon is absent, since only M_{0,3} is involved; the resulting group is what the literature sometimes calls GT^_0 / the 'genus 0, n = 3 part'. The derivation comes from the S_3-equivariance of automorphisms of pi^_{0,3} normalising inertia, apparently in the early 1980s, before Drinfeld 1990.

Next page. The adelic computation pushes xi and eta into SL(2,Z^) via the Gamma(2) picture of pi_{0,3}. This is used to fix nu and to prove that 2nu+1 is invertible.
errors: The equation number (145) is used twice; the second should be (146).
The label after (141) is (143) in the manuscript (it reads like (142)/(143)), and (144) follows with no (143) visible, so the numbering is irregular.

The claim that mu is determined by xi alone is only sketched ('comme le montrent les calculs abéliens...'). It is plausible because xi = eta l_1^{nu} need not lie in the commutator subgroup, so abelianisation detects nu, but no proof is given on this page.

For 'il faut et il suffit' in (144), sufficiency is clear. Necessity requires that the ambiguity in the lift is exactly the normaliser/centraliser contribution from L_0; this relies on earlier pages (centraliser of S_3-type elements in pi^ being trivial modulo L_0) and is not rechecked here.

Verification of the elimination: from (xi l_1^{-nu}) sigma_infinity(xi l_1^{-nu}) = 1 and sigma_infinity(l_1) = l_0 one gets sigma_infinity(xi) = l_1^nu xi^{-1} l_0^nu, as written. This is consistent.

ideas.what: Group structure on cocycle pairs (xi, eta) given by (xi', eta')(xi, eta) = (u'(xi) xi', u'(eta) eta')
ideas.modern_name: Composition law of GT^ (Drinfeld's multiplication on pairs (lambda, f))
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse (which mentions the Teichmüller tower and the action of Gal(Qbar/Q) but gives no formulas)

ideas.what: Every automorphism commuting with S_3 up to inner equals int(f^{-1}) composed with u_{(xi,eta)}, unique up to the L_0-action
ideas.modern_name: Lifting of GT^ elements to automorphisms of F^_2; coboundary change of normalised cocycles

ideas.what: Elimination to a single unknown satisfying eta sigma(eta) = 1 and the twisted 3-cycle relation (eta l_1^nu) rho(...) rho^2(...) = 1, with lambda = 2nu+1
ideas.modern_name: Drinfeld's defining relations (I) and (II) of GT^, i.e. the group GT^_0 without the pentagon
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990 ('On quasitriangular quasi-Hopf algebras and a group closely connected with Gal(Qbar/Q)')
ideas.where_published: Unpublished Montpellier notes (sequel to La Longue Marche, 1981)

ideas.what: The multiplier mu/nu is determined by xi alone, via abelian/congruence computations in GL(2,Z^)'
ideas.modern_name: lambda is determined by f (injectivity of GT^ -> F^_2, or its 0,3 analogue)

missed.claim: Grothendieck derives, independently of and apparently well before Drinfeld (1990), the two-cycle and three-cycle (hexagon) relations that define GT^. He gets them from S_3-equivariant automorphisms of pi^_{0,3} normalising inertia, with the multiplier written as 2nu+1, exactly like Drinfeld's lambda = 2m+1.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and documentation: shows Grothendieck had the explicit genus-0, 3-point part of GT^ (GT^_0) with its group law. Specialists suspect this, but it is not documented in the literature.

missed.claim: Claim (pursued on the next pages) that the multiplier is determined by xi alone and that invertibility of 2nu+1 follows from the relations themselves, via adelic computations in SL(2,Z^) through the Gamma(2)/congruence picture. In Drinfeld's definition lambda in Z^* is imposed as an axiom.
missed.quote: μ est déjà déterminé de façon unique par la seule connaissance de ξ, comme le montrent les calculs abéliens dans Gl(2,Ẑ)'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: If correct, it shows that the condition lambda in Z^* in the definition of GT^_0 is redundant, and it gives a congruence-subgroup (SL_2(Z^)) method to study GT^_0. Worth checking against the known literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page explicitly writes the Drinfeld GT^ relations (I) and (II), with the 2nu+1 multiplier and the group law, in unpublished early-1980s notes. That is a notable priority detail, though the GT^ connection to Grothendieck's program is widely acknowledged and the pentagon is absent here.
transcription_corrections: 'cet en fait μ' should read 'et en fait μ'.

'on peut éliminer l'une ou l'autre des systèmes d'équations (133),(134), qui devient' should read roughly 'on peut éliminer l'une ou l'autre [inconnue], et le système d'équations (133),(134) devient'.
The second '(145)' is (146) in the manuscript.
The equation after (141) is labelled (143) in the image, not (142).
In 'il faut et il suffit [?]' the reading 'il faut et il suffit' is correct.
The corollary concerns u ∈ M_{0,3}^{!~} (automorphisms), with f ∈ Π^_{0,3}; 'u_{(ξ,η)}' is correct.
